claim: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinases (IP6Ks) are emerging as relevant pharmacological targets because a multitude of disease-related phenotypes has been associated with their function.
source: Inositol hexakisphosphate kinases (IP6Ks) are emerging as relevant pharmacological targets because a multitude of disease-related phenotypes has been associated with their function.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to established scientific literature about IP6K functions in disease contexts.

claim: A pharmacological tool to distinguish the mammalian isozymes is still lacking.
source: While the development of potent IP6K inhibitors is gaining momentum, a pharmacological tool to distinguish the mammalian isozymes is still lacking.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the current state of research.

claim: FMP-201300 exhibited high potency and selectivity toward the unique valine gatekeeper mutants of IP6K1 and IP6K2, compared to the respective wild-type (WT) kinases.
source: The most promising hit, FMP-201300, exhibited high potency and selectivity toward the unique valine gatekeeper mutants of IP6K1 and IP6K2, compared to the respective wild-type (WT) kinases.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the high-throughput screen and validation experiments.

claim: Biochemical validation experiments revealed an allosteric mechanism of action for FMP-201300.
source: Biochemical validation experiments revealed an allosteric mechanism of action that was corroborated by hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry measurements.
evidence: This is supported by Lineweaver-Burk plots and HDX-MS measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: Displacement of the αC helix, caused by the gatekeeper mutation, facilitates the binding of FMP-201300 to an allosteric pocket adjacent to the ATP-binding site.
source: The latter analysis suggested that displacement of the αC helix, caused by the gatekeeper mutation, facilitates the binding of FMP-201300 to an allosteric pocket adjacent to the ATP-binding site.
evidence: This is based on HDX-MS data analysis and inference from structural changes.

claim: PP-InsPs have emerged as a group of ubiquitous small molecule messengers with pivotal functions in cellular homeostasis, metabolism, and many disease-related signaling events.
source: Over the last decades, inositol pyrophosphates (PP-InsPs) have emerged as a group of ubiquitous small molecule messengers with pivotal functions in cellular homeostasis, metabolism, and many disease-related signaling events (Mukherjee et al., 2020; Chakraborty, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Genetic knockouts of the three mammalian IP6K isozymes have revealed their involvement in distinct biological processes, including insulin signaling, apoptosis, cancer metastasis, and lifespan regulation in mice.
source: Genetic knockouts of the three mammalian inositol hexakisphosphate kinase (IP6K) isozymes – enzymes involved in PP-InsP biosynthesis – have revealed their involvement in distinct biological processes, including insulin signaling (Bhandari et al., 2008; Manning, 2010; Chakraborty et al., 2010), apoptosis (Rao et al., 2014; Koldobskiy et al., 2010; Morrison et al., 2001), cancer metastasis (Rao et al., 2015), and lifespan regulation in mice (Moritoh et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: Knockdown of IP6K1, but not IP6K2, inhibited the exocytosis of insulin-containing granules in pancreatic beta cells.
source: For example, knockdown of IP6K1, but not IP6K2, inhibited the exocytosis of insulin-containing granules in pancreatic beta cells (Illies et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Deletion of IP6K2, but not the other two IP6K isozymes, reduced cell death.
source: In another instance deletion of IP6K2, but not the other two IP6K isozymes, reduced cell death (Nagata et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Genetic experiments perturbing IP6K function can be accompanied by compensatory effects and secondary genetic changes.
source: Although genetic experiments perturbing IP6K function have contributed significantly to our understanding of PP-InsP signaling, these studies can be accompanied by compensatory effects and secondary genetic changes.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a study showing confounding results.

claim: The undesired transcriptional up- and downregulation of numerous genes has caused confounding results in the past.
source: The undesired transcriptional up- and downregulation of numerous genes has caused confounding results in the past (Worley et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Genetic knockout inevitably abolishes the non-catalytic functions of the kinase, which, under some circumstances, are essential for the regulation of specific cellular processes.
source: Furthermore, genetic knockout inevitably abolishes the non-catalytic functions of the kinase, which, under some circumstances, are essential for the regulation of specific cellular processes (Koldobskiy et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2001; Zhu et al., 2016; Chakraborty et al., 2008; Fu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The generation of single point kinase-dead mutants usually warrants correct protein expression and folding, but can be accompanied by notable transcriptional alterations.
source: The generation of single point kinase-dead mutants usually warrants correct protein expression and folding, but can be accompanied by notable transcriptional alterations (Worley et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The rapid interconversion of PP-InsPs in cells indicates fast signal transmission.
source: Lastly, a limitation of genetic approaches is the long timeframe, which can lead to genetic compensation (El-Brolosy and Stainier, 2017) and appears inherently incompatible with the rapid interconversion of PP-InsPs in cells, indicating fast signal transmission (Menniti et al., 1993; Glennon and Shears, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on PP-InsP dynamics.

claim: TNP has lost appreciation due to the accumulation of unfavorable properties.
source: While the benchmark inhibitor N2-(m-trifluorobenzyl)-N6-(p-nitrobenzyl)purine (TNP; Padmanabhan et al., 2009; Figure 1b) has lost appreciation due to the accumulation of unfavorable properties (Zhu et al., 2017; Chang et al., 2002; Stork and Li, 2010), the development of novel pharmacological tools targeting IP6Ks has recently picked up speed (Kröber et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies documenting TNP's limitations.

claim: High-throughput screens and structure-guided design have yielded compounds with low nanomolar potencies, such as SC-919.
source: High-throughput screens and structure-guided design have yielded compounds with low nanomolar potencies, such as SC-919 (Moritoh et al., 2021; Terao et al., 2018; Figure 1b) and others (Zhou et al., 2022; Liao et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies and reference to Figure 1b.

claim: With the exception of one isozyme-selective inhibitor targeting IP6K1 (Barrow-24), all other IP6K inhibitors lack specificity.
source: However, with the exception of one isozyme-selective inhibitor targeting IP6K1 (Barrow-24; Wormald et al., 2019; Figure 1b), all other IP6K inhibitors lack specificity.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1b.

claim: The analog-sensitive approach enables the generation of mutually selective kinase-inhibitor pairs.
source: To achieve selective kinase inhibition, Shokat and co-workers developed the analog-sensitive approach, which enables the generation of mutually selective kinase-inhibitor pairs (Bishop et al., 1998; Lopez et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the original work by Shokat and colleagues.

claim: A conserved medium- to large-sized gatekeeper residue is mutated to glycine or alanine in the analog-sensitive approach, thereby creating an additional pocket in the ATP-binding site that does not occur in any other wild-type kinase.
source: A conserved medium- to large-sized gatekeeper residue is mutated to glycine or alanine, thereby creating an additional pocket in the ATP-binding site that does not occur in any other wild-type (WT) kinase.
evidence: This describes the established methodology of the analog-sensitive approach.

claim: Designed inhibitor analogs with a sterically demanding substituent fit into the enlarged ATP-binding site but clash with the active site of WT kinases.
source: While designed inhibitor analogs with a sterically demanding substituent fit into the enlarged ATP-binding site, they clash with the active site of WT kinases (Bishop et al., 1998; Bishop et al., 1999; Liu et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational studies on the analog-sensitive approach.

claim: Implementation of the analog-sensitive method for various kinase families of multiple organisms has provided remarkable insight into the function and regulation of phosphorylation-based signaling.
source: Implementation of this method for various kinase families of multiple organisms has provided remarkable insight into the function and regulation of phosphorylation-based signaling (Liu et al., 2004; Sreenivasan et al., 2003; Carroll et al., 2001; Weiss et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous applications of the method.

claim: The analog-sensitive approach has been applied to over 80 protein kinases.
source: While the analog-sensitive approach has been applied to over 80 protein kinases, the implementation for kinases phosphorylating small molecules, such as lipids or sugars, proved more challenging and has received scant attention to date.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact about the application of the method.

claim: Mutation of the gatekeeper residue in S. cerevisiae VPS34 yielded an active mutant allele, however, mutation of the mammalian PI3K p110α gatekeeper resulted in a drastic decline of kinase activity.
source: For example, mutation of the gatekeeper residue in S. cerevisiae VPS34, a PI3 kinase, yielded an active mutant allele, however, mutation of the mammalian PI3K p110α gatekeeper resulted in a drastic decline of kinase activity (Alaimo et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: PI3K-like kinase TOR2 from S. cerevisiae was sensitized to the mTOR inhibitor BEZ235 by mutating its gatekeeper residue to alanine.
source: A similar observation was made with PI3K-like kinase TOR2 from S. cerevisiae, which was sensitized to the mTOR inhibitor BEZ235 by mutating its gatekeeper residue to alanine.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The mammalian kinase mTOR was rendered catalytically inactive by the same mutation.
source: The mammalian kinase mTOR, on the other hand, was rendered catalytically inactive by the same mutation (Kliegman et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The gatekeeper identification in inositol phosphate (InsP) kinases is facilitated by the structural similarity of their active site architecture to protein kinases.
source: The gatekeeper identification in inositol phosphate (InsP) kinases is facilitated by the structural similarity of their active site architecture to protein kinases (Randall et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The gatekeeper residues of the human IP6K isozymes are Leu210, Leu206, and Leu201 for IP6K1, IP6K2, and IP6K3, respectively.
source: Owing to the decent sequence similarity within the active site, the gatekeeper residues of the human IP6K isozymes could be identified by simple sequence alignment with the abovementioned related InsP kinases and are Leu210, Leu206, and Leu201 for IP6K1, IP6K2, and IP6K3, respectively (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The gatekeeper mutants L210G and L210A of IP6K1 were not tolerated and rendered the protein virtually inactive.
source: Unfortunately, both the alanine and glycine mutations were not tolerated by IP6K1 and rendered the protein virtually inactive (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: IP6K2 suffered a drastic decline in substrate turnover upon gatekeeper mutation to glycine.
source: Likewise, IP6K2 suffered a drastic decline in substrate turnover upon gatekeeper mutation to glycine (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The valine gatekeeper mutant completely retained its catalytic activity compared to the WT enzyme.
source: Unlike the previous mutations, the valine gatekeeper mutant completely retained its catalytic activity compared to the WT enzyme and was thus further investigated (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The KM value of IP6K1wt for ATP was determined as 186 ± 23 µM.
source: The KM value of IP6K1wt was determined as 186 ± 23 µM and is in good accordance with the literature (Harmel et al., 2019; Wormald et al., 2017; Wundenberg et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements and citations to previous studies.

claim: The valine gatekeeper mutation resulted in a twofold reduction in ATP affinity (KM = 412 ± 81 µM) along with a 60% increase in vmax from 300 to 480 nmol min−1 mg−1.
source: We observed a twofold reduction in ATP affinity (KM = 412 ± 81 µM) along with a 60% increase in vmax from 300 to 480 nmol min−1 mg−1, implicating a faster substrate conversion despite impaired ATP binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental kinetic measurements.

claim: The valine mutation seems to exacerbate the substrate inhibition.
source: The valine mutation also seems to exacerbate the substrate inhibition, which complicates the comparison of these steady-state parameters and suggests a change in protein dynamics upon gatekeeper mutation.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental observations of kinetic behavior.

claim: Established analog-sensitive kinase inhibitors exhibited no inhibitory activity against IP6K1wt at 10 µM concentration.
source: As expected, none of these compounds exhibited any inhibitory activity against IP6K1wt at 10 µM concentration (Figure 2e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Established analog-sensitive kinase inhibitors did not inhibit IP6K1L210V.
source: However, inhibition of IP6K1L210V was not observed either, making these molecules unsuitable as inhibitors for analog-sensitive IP6Ks.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental screening data.

claim: A high-throughput screen encompassing 54,912 small molecule inhibitors and inhibitor-like structures was performed.
source: Seeking to identify an inhibitor selective for the gatekeeper mutant, IP6K1wt and IP6K1L210V were submitted to a high-throughput screen encompassing 54,912 small molecule inhibitors and inhibitor-like structures (Lisurek et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The reverse reaction of IP6K1 with the Kinase-Glo assay converts 5PP-InsP5 and ADP to InsP6 and ATP.
source: Nevertheless, we were able to take advantage of these properties by examining the reverse reaction of IP6K1 with the Kinase-Glo assay, where 5PP-InsP5 and ADP are converted to InsP6 and ATP (Figure 3a).
evidence: This describes the assay methodology used in the screen.

claim: An excellent Z′-factor of 0.81 was achieved indicating high assay quality and feasibility.
source: An excellent Z′-factor (Zhang et al., 1999) of 0.81 was achieved indicating high assay quality and feasibility.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental validation data.

claim: The pilot screen confirmed the suitability of the final screening setup by yielding known IP6K inhibitors myricetin and 6-hydroxy-dl-DOPA.
source: It confirmed the suitability of the final screening setup by yielding known IP6K inhibitors myricetin and 6-hydroxy-dl-DOPA (Wormald et al., 2017; Gu et al., 2019) and displaying good hit reproducibility as depicted in the Bland–Altmann plot (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b; Martin Bland and Altman, 1986).
evidence: This claim is supported by pilot screen results and citations to previous studies.

claim: The high-throughput screen identified 258 putative hits (0.5% hit rate) after applying specific thresholds.
source: Putative hits for the gatekeeper mutant were subsequently identified by excluding compounds with a z-score higher than −4 and a residual activity greater than 80% (Figure 3b). The remaining 258 compounds (0.5% hit rate) were retested in a dose-dependent reconfirmation and counter screen (see SI for details) to eliminate random false positives (compounds that do not confirm activity) and chemical false positives (compounds directly interfering with the assay readout).
evidence: This claim is supported by the screening data and analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claim: 178 inhibitors were classified as true hits after eliminating false positives.
source: This analysis uncovered 80 molecules as false positives, while 178 inhibitors were consequently classified true hits.
evidence: This claim is supported by the screening data analysis.

claim: The majority of mutant-selective inhibitors were dietary flavonoids such as quercetin and fisetin.
source: Curiously, the majority of mutant-selective inhibitors were dietary flavonoids such as quercetin and fisetin (Supplementary file 1; Gu et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by screening results and a citation.

claim: Flavonoids are promiscuous ATP-competitive inhibitors with various off-target effects.
source: Since flavonoids are promiscuous ATP-competitive inhibitors with various off-target effects (Xue et al., 2017; Navarro-Retamal et al., 2016; Wright et al., 2013; Russo et al., 2017; Walker et al., 2000), and the compounds had been flagged as pan-assay interference compounds (PAINS) based on structural filters (Baell and Nissink, 2018), they were deemed unsuitable as selective IP6K inhibitors and thus not investigated further.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies on flavonoid properties.

claim: FMP-201300 displayed good selectivity for the gatekeeper mutant with IC50 values of 17 and 1.6 µM against IP6K1wt and IP6K1L210V, respectively.
source: The only non-polyphenolic molecule, FMP-201300, displayed good selectivity for the gatekeeper mutant with IC50 values of 17 and 1.6 µM against IP6K1wt and IP6K1L210V, respectively (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental IC50 measurements shown in Figure 3d.

claim: FMP-201300 has no known inhibitory activities against other biological targets.
source: Importantly, the almost symmetrical inhibitor has no known inhibitory activities against other biological targets and does not display any recognized PAINS motifs (Baell and Nissink, 2018).
evidence: This is stated based on literature searches and structural analysis.

claim: FMP-201300 was neither redox-active, nor cytotoxic, against HEK293 or HepG2 cell lines at a concentration of 10 µM.
source: Furthermore, FMP-201300 was neither redox-active, nor cytotoxic, against HEK293 or HepG2 cell lines at a concentration of 10 µM (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental toxicity testing data.

claim: The NMR assay confirmed FMP-201300 as a potent and mutant-selective inhibitor with IC50 values of 114 and 810 nM for IP6K1L210V and IP6K1wt, respectively.
source: The assay confirmed FMP-201300 as a potent and mutant-selective inhibitor with IC50 values of 114 and 810 nM for IP6K1L210V and IP6K1wt, respectively (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental NMR assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: FMP-201300 was 11 times more potent against IP6K2L206V compared to IP6K2wt with IC50 values of 190 nM and 2.14 µM, respectively.
source: FMP-201300 was 11 time more potent against IP6K2L206V compared to IP6K2wt with IC50 values of 190 nM and 2.14 µM, respectively (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental IC50 measurements shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The evolutionarily related ortholog IP6KA from Entamoeba histolytica was sensitized to inhibition by FMP-201300 when its methionine gatekeeper was mutated to valine.
source: However, the evolutionarily related ortholog IP6KA from Entamoeba histolytica (Eh) was sensitized to inhibition by FMP-201300 when its methionine gatekeeper was mutated to valine (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: None of the FMP-201300 analogs (A1–A4) inhibited IP6K1L210V by more than 30% at 10 µM concentration.
source: Interestingly, none of the analogs inhibited the kinase by more than 30%.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental testing of analogs shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Analog A1, which was merely lacking the carboxylic acid groups, was completely inactive.
source: Although A1 was merely lacking the carboxylic acid groups, it was completely inactive.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental testing of analogs.

claim: The carboxylic acid appears to be indispensable for inhibitory activity.
source: Hence, the carboxylic acid appears to be indispensable for inhibitory activity and is likely engaged in pivotal interactions at the inhibitor-binding site.
evidence: This is inferred from structure-activity relationship data.

claim: Lineweaver–Burk measurements revealed a clear allosteric mechanism for FMP-201300.
source: Surprisingly, these measurements revealed a clear allosteric mechanism for FMP-201300 (Figure 4d).
evidence: This claim is supported by Lineweaver-Burk plot data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: TNP exhibited an unambiguous competitive mechanism of action.
source: In agreement with the literature, the results indicated an unambiguous competitive mechanism of action for TNP (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by Lineweaver-Burk plot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2a.

claim: TNP exhibited no significant difference in potency against IP6K1wt and IP6K1L210V.
source: In addition, TNP exhibited no significant difference in potency against IP6K1wt and IP6K1L210V, again pointing toward a different inhibitory mechanism of FMP-201300 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental IC50 data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The difference in IC50 values measured at 100 and 500 µM InsP6 concentration was negligible, excluding substrate inhibition as a potential mechanism.
source: However, the difference in IC50 values measured at 100 and 500 µM InsP6 concentration was negligible, excluding substrate inhibition as a potential mechanism (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental IC50 measurements at different substrate concentrations shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Major decreases in deuterium exchange rates were observed in proximity to the ATP-binding site upon FMP-201300 binding to IP6K1L210V.
source: Major decreases in exchange rates were observed in proximity to the ATP-binding site, whereas remote sites were mostly unaltered (Figure 5a and Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS experimental data shown in Figure 5a and Figure 5—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Amino acid residues 40–45, 67–79, and 205–212, corresponding to β strands 1–3, and residues 53–58 within the αC helix of IP6K1, exhibited large decreases in deuterium exchange rates upon FMP-201300 binding.
source: Amino acid residues 40–45, 67–79, and 205–212, corresponding to β strands 1–3, and residues 53–58 within the αC helix of IP6K1, exhibited large decreases in deuterium exchange rates.
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS experimental data.

claim: The leucine to valine gatekeeper mutation led to increases in HD exchange in the β2–β3 strands and αC helix, indicating an overall increased flexibility in this region.
source: The leucine to valine mutation led to increases in HD exchange in the β2–β3 strands and αC helix, indicating an overall increased flexibility in this region (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data comparing WT and mutant shown in Figure 5.

claim: The L210V gatekeeper mutation of IP6Ks putatively causes a displacement of the αC helix sufficient to expand a pocket adjacent to the ATP-binding site, which sensitizes the kinase to an allosteric inhibitor.
source: In conclusion, the L210V gatekeeper mutation of IP6Ks putatively causes a displacement of the αC helix sufficient to expand a pocket adjacent to the ATP-binding site, which sensitizes the kinase to an allosteric inhibitor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from HDX-MS data and kinetic measurements.

claim: A subtle leucine to valine mutation did not perturb the kinase activity.
source: While the conventional glycine and alanine gatekeeper mutants suffered a drastic decline in catalytic efficiency, a subtle leucine to valine mutation did not perturb the kinase activity.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the Results section.

claim: FMP-201300 had not been assigned any function in previous screens and displayed no toxicity in cell culture.
source: The compound had not been assigned any function in previous screens and displayed no toxicity in cell culture.
evidence: This is stated based on literature searches and experimental toxicity testing.

claim: FMP-201300 was able to recapitulate the reduction of ribosomal RNA synthesis phenotype, indicating sufficient crossing of the cell membrane.
source: The inhibitor, alongside two established IP6K inhibitors, was able to recapitulate this recently reported phenotype (Morgan et al., 2022), indicating sufficient crossing of the cell membrane despite its two carboxylic acids.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental cellular assay data and a citation.

claim: Other carboxylate-containing IP6K inhibitors had proven efficacious in cellula and in vivo before.
source: In fact, other carboxylate-containing IP6K inhibitors had proven efficacious in cellula and in vivo before (Moritoh et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A wide range of bioisosteres, including hydroxamic acids, sulfonamides, tetrazoles, and others, would be available to circumvent potential issues arising with FMP-201300.
source: Regardless, a wide range of bioisosteres, including hydroxamic acids, sulfonamides, tetrazoles, and others (Ballatore et al., 2013), would be available to circumvent potential issues arising with FMP-201300.
evidence: This is based on established medicinal chemistry knowledge and a citation.

claim: The structures of the WT and mutant EhIP6KA are virtually identical except for the additional space generated by the reduced gatekeeper size.
source: Remarkably, the structures of the WT and mutant EhIP6KA are virtually identical except for the additional space generated by the reduced gatekeeper size (Figure 4—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1d.

claim: A loss in activity was observed for roughly 30% of all examined protein kinases upon introduction of a space-creating gatekeeper mutation.
source: In fact, a loss in activity was observed for roughly 30% of all examined protein kinases (Zhang et al., 2005) and has proven particularly detrimental for small molecule kinases, such as the phosphoinositide lipid kinases (Alaimo et al., 2005; Kliegman et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Shokat and co-workers identified second-site suppressor mutations that rescue the catalytic activity of some kinases sensitive to the reduction in gatekeeper size.
source: To address this challenge, Shokat and co-workers identified second-site suppressor mutations that rescue the catalytic activity of some kinases sensitive to the reduction in gatekeeper size (Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The majority of kinases in the human kinome carry medium- to large-sized gatekeeper residues, such as methionine, tyrosine, or phenylalanine.
source: While the substitution of leucine with valine was comparatively subtle, the majority of kinases in the human kinome carry medium- to large-sized gatekeeper residues, such as methionine, tyrosine, or phenylalanine (Zuccotto et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study on kinome gatekeeper residues.

claim: The greater heterogeneity of residues and conformations in allosteric pockets could pave the way for isozyme-selective IP6K inhibitors that do not require chemical genetic engineering.
source: The greater heterogeneity of residues and conformations in allosteric pockets (Lu et al., 2014), even in isozymes of the same kinase, could pave the way for isozyme-selective IP6K inhibitors that do not require chemical genetic engineering.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on a citation and inference from the results.

claim: Binding of FMP-201300 to a hydrophobic pocket adjacent to the ATP site, which is generated by αC helix displacement, seems plausible and is an established mode of action for allosteric kinase inhibitors.
source: Binding of FMP-201300 to a hydrophobic pocket adjacent to the ATP site, which is generated by αC helix displacement, seems plausible and is an established mode of action for allosteric kinase inhibitors (Palmieri and Rastelli, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and a citation to previous work on allosteric inhibitors.

claim: A similar phenomenon was observed for an allosteric EGFR inhibitor that was 1000-fold more potent against the acquired T790M gatekeeper resistance mutant, compared to the WT kinase.
source: The first scenario appears more likely, as a similar phenomenon was observed for an allosteric EGFR inhibitor that was 1000-fold more potent against the acquired T790M gatekeeper resistance mutant, compared to the WT kinase (Jia et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on EGFR inhibitors.

claim: The EGFR inhibitor exhibited direct binding interaction with the mutated gatekeeper residue, similar to observations with FMP-201300.
source: The EGFR inhibitor also exhibited direct binding interaction with the mutated gatekeeper residue, similar to our observations with FMP-201300.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the current results with previous studies.

claim: Allosteric inhibitors preferably target an inactive conformation of protein kinases, which often confers selectivity owing to their greater structural heterogeneity compared to the corresponding active conformations.
source: In general, these allosteric inhibitors preferably target an inactive conformation of protein kinases, which often confers selectivity owing to their greater structural heterogeneity compared to the corresponding active conformations (Laufkötter et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work on allosteric inhibitors.

claim: FMP-201300 constitutes a valuable addition to the ever-growing group of IP6K inhibitors and serves as an intriguing starting point for further characterization and improvement.
source: As of now, FMP-201300 constitutes a valuable addition to the ever-growing group of IP6K inhibitors and serves as an intriguing starting point for further characterization and improvement.
evidence: This is a concluding statement based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: FMP-201300 could provide a springboard for the heavily sought-after isozyme-selective inhibition of mammalian IP6Ks, either as analog-sensitive kinase inhibitor or allosteric lead compound for the development of inhibitors against the WT kinases.
source: It could provide a springboard for the heavily sought-after isozyme-selective inhibition of mammalian IP6Ks, either as analog-sensitive kinase inhibitor or allosteric lead compound for the development of inhibitors against the WT kinases.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications based on the current findings.
